signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Tightening + Positioning Divergence
signals.text: US headline September CPI printed at 3.7% year-over-year versus 3.6% expected, reigniting Federal Reserve hike pricing ahead of the 28 October FOMC. In policy terms, Fed at 4.00% (HIKING) versus ECB at 2.65% (HIKING) maintains a 135bp nominal policy spread and a +145bp SOFR/€STR carry advantage favoring USD. Intraday price action holds EUR/USD down at 1.1198, tracking well below its SMA20 (1.1312), SMA50 (1.1484), and SMA200 (1.1595) moving average stack. CFTC data shows institutional leveraged funds heavily short EUR at net -84,775 contracts (pctl 4, z -1.64), while retail accounts sit heavily long at 87% on Retail sentiment data, creating an acute positioning divergence vulnerable to further downside liquidation. Macro rate differentials and institutional momentum firmly favor USD extension across the curve. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; macro carry spread and institutional short trend suppress spot rallies. Catalyst: Euro Area final CPI release on 15 October at 09:00 UTC. Risk: US Retail Sales print below forecast on 15 October, stalling USD upside momentum.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.90, positioned above its SMA20 at 157.75 and SMA50 at 157.72, while holding below the 200-day moving average at 158.49. Nominal central bank policy rates of Fed 4.00% versus BoJ 1.25% establish a +275bp policy advantage for the dollar, reinforced by a +266bp SOFR versus TONA carry spread. Despite this structural carry buffer, the options market exhibits acute caution with 1-month 25-delta Risk Reversals printing at -1.70, reflecting elevated demand for JPY call and USD put downside protection. In parallel, implied volatility trades at 7.6% against a 30-day realized volatility of 9.5%, leaving a negative Vol Risk Premium of -1.9% that signals compressed volatility pricing ahead of the 160.00 watch level. While the carry return keeps the pair structurally supported, intervention vigilance caps unhedged upside participation. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; steady carry returns offset by pronounced options downside hedging. Catalyst: BoJ policy decision on 30 October. Risk: USD/JPY clears and holds above 158.50 on accelerating momentum, invalidating the options put skew.

signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: Weekly G10 currency performance establishes NOK as the primary outperformer with an average gain of +0.792% across two pairs, while EUR lags the complex at -0.271% across nine pairs, producing a bilateral spread of 1.063%. Norges Bank maintains an aggressive policy setting at 4.50% (HIKING) against ECB at 2.65% (HIKING), yielding a substantial 185bp policy differential in favor of the krone. Macro fundamentals reinforce the divergence as Norway exhibits a restrictive real policy rate of +1.82% backed by a +13.1 Economic Surprise Index reading, contrasting with the softer European economic backdrop. EUR/NOK spot trading at 10.6233 sits notably discounted against its BEER fair-value model benchmark of 10.8463 (z -2.76σ), reflecting acute market misvaluation. The combination of G10 relative strength and wide interest-rate support keeps NOK bid against European crosses. Trade bias: Bullish NOK against EUR; weekly performance leadership underpinned by 185bp carry buffer. Catalyst: Euro Area Industrial Production print on 15 October at 09:00 UTC. Risk: Sharp decline in crude prices below $90/bbl, eroding NOK terms of trade support.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Compression Ahead of Labour Print
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6980, compressed below its critical moving average confluence with SMA20 at 0.7010, SMA50 at 0.7088, and SMA200 at 0.7042. RBA policy at 4.60% (HIKING) versus Fed 4.00% (HIKING) maintains an active 60bp nominal carry premium for the Australian dollar, reflected in a -71bp SOFR/AONIA spread. Leveraged funds hold net long positioning of +48,911 contracts, though a WoW reduction of -6,203 contracts highlights momentum consolidation at the upper percentile band (pctl 67, z +0.58). Options market skew mirrors this tactical caution, with 1-month 25-delta Risk Reversals printing at -0.85 put skew while ATM implied volatility at 7.1% runs +1.1% over HV30 at 6.0%. Technical compression below 0.7000 leaves spot price highly sensitive to near-term domestic employment shocks. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; technical overhead resistance counters structural carry advantage. Catalyst: Australia Employment Change report on 15 October at 00:30 UTC. Risk: Australia unemployment rate prints higher than 4.6%, breaking spot below 0.6950 support.
